citation: Hernández J.A., Larrabeiti D., Otero Pérez G., Fernández-Palacios J.P. (2021) PASSION WDM planner, deliverable D6.7. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4838021.
description: The PASSION WDM planner is a software tool for designing and planning metro optical networks that use the photonic hardware developed in the European PASSION project, written by José Alberto Hernández, David Larrabeiti, Gabriel Otero Pérez and Juan Pedro Fernández-Palacios of Universidad Carlos III de Madrid and Telefónica and published as project deliverable D6.7 in May 2021. Written in R with the igraph library, it takes the optical characterisation of the hardware for optical signal-to-noise calculations, a hierarchical network topology and a traffic matrix, and computes disjoint primary and backup lightpaths from edge nodes to core nodes, wavelength assignment per fibre link and techno-economic results including per-node design and inventory cost under a pay-as-you-grow model. Coverage: generic metro networks; any topology can be supplied. Format and access: R source code on Zenodo, free under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Caveats: tied to the PASSION hardware assumptions; a research deliverable, not maintained. Simulation uses: capacity planning and optimisation of metro optical networks with protection paths, and cost studies. Related records: the SEASON and Telefónica reference topologies give input networks.
